subject: Stream termination during PoC — SDK early cutoffs (triage + product ask)
messages:
From: Sarah Chen <s.chen@quantumai.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Park <alex.park@finflow.io>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SDK stream cutting off mid-response during PoC

Hey Vivek,

Quick note from the PoC today — several of our long-turn examples (multi-step reasoning) are being cut off partway through the model response. The UI shows the SDK stream as closed, but the model log on your dashboard shows the inference completed. This creates mismatched state: we sometimes miss the last 20–60 tokens.

Repro steps (simple):
- Start streaming completion with prompt size ~1.8k tokens + streaming=true
- Let it run ~10–20s until a nested generation step triggers
- Observe client receives <END_STREAM> earlier than model completion (we captured timings)

I've attached a short sample log (sample_stream_log.txt) and a zipped error trace. This is blocking our evaluation for the integration. Can the runtime team triage? If there is a known SDK flag we can toggle on our end as a temporary workaround, please let me know.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Chen
Sr. ML Engineer, QuantumAI

Thanks for the detailed repro, Sarah — really helpful. Looping in Sean and Logan from runtime/serving so we can get a quick triage. I copied Alex too since FinFlow is on the integration path and may have seen similar behaviors.

Initial asks from our side:
- Can you share a minimal client snippet you used to open the stream? (headers + any SDK options)
- Confirm whether you saw a transport-level close (FIN) vs. an application-level termination event in your client logs.

Temporary mitigation: we've seen a similar symptom when the client idle timeout interacts with our prefix caching — increasing the client-side keepalive/idle timeout (if configurable) to 45s has helped other PoCs. That isn't ideal.

I'll schedule a 30-min triage today if that works for everyone — ping me preferred times. Logan: can you start by looking at the attached logs?

-Vivek

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Sarah Chen <s.chen@quantumai.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SDK stream cutting off mid-response during PoC

Thanks — I pulled the attached sample_stream_log.txt and the trace. Preliminary notes:

- The runtime logs show the model completing and emitting the final token batch at t=00:00:15.322.
- The client stream connection receives a CLOSE event at t=00:00:15.124 — ~200ms earlier.
- TcpDump on the edge indicates a keepalive ACK but no explicit FIN from the client at that moment (suggests SDK may be closing the stream proactively).

Likely root causes (hypothesis):
1) SDK-side premature termination when incremental delta has low throughput (client-side heuristic thinks generation finished). We saw similar heuristics in old SDK versions that attempted to coalesce short gaps into an EOF.
2) A mismatch between our stream idle-threshold and the SDK's default read-timeout. The SDK default we ship is 15s idle. If the client experiences a 16s gap during internal reroute, it may assume the server is done.

Immediate actions I'll take:
- Reproduce locally with your snippet (please paste it) and try toggling the read-timeout to 45s.
- Prepare a minimal patch to the TypeScript and Python SDKs to expose an explicit keepalive/read-timeout option and a server-side "defer-close" hint. I attached a draft patch sdk-fix-keepalive-draft.diff with a proposed API: streamOptions: { readTimeoutMs, preferServerClose }

Longer-term product ask (for roadmap discussion):
- Expose a server-side handshake flag that lets SDKs know whether the server may emit delayed final batches (e.g., due to KV cache merge or rerouting). "preferServerClose" would default false for backward compatibility. If product likes this we can prioritize in Q4.

Sarah — can you paste the snippet and confirm whether you used our JS SDK or a custom HTTP client? Also, any additional traces from the browser console would help.

-Logan
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SDK stream cutting off mid-response during PoC

Appreciate the quick triage. From AE/SE side — this is high impact for the QuantumAI deal (HS-48291). A few asks I'd like product/eng to consider during the triage:

- Expose a supported SDK knob (server/backed) so customers don't have to patch transports. Many enterprise clients route through proxies that add jitter; having an opt-in server hint will be easier for customers.
- Gap communication: customers need deterministic behavior for streaming vs completions. If we change defaults, we should publish a compatibility note and migration steps.

Proposed mutual action plan for the next 7 days:
[ ] Logan: confirm repro and provide temporary SDK flag we can ship as a hotfix (TS/Python).
[ ] Vivek: coordinate customer test window and get minimal snippet from Sarah.
[ ] Product: evaluate "preferServerClose" as a shortlist item for Q4 roadmap (if product approves, I'll add to deal docs as a potential value-add).
[ ] Legal/Procurement (QuantumAI): expedite any security questionnaires if we need to push a patch across their environment.

Sarah, can you commit to a 30-min test tomorrow morning (10am PT) so we can validate the workaround? I'll put a calendar invite once we agree.

-Marissa
